title: Short special meeting adjourns development charge complaints
subtitle: Closed session on potential litigation, March 2 meeting moved to 4 p.m., and routine by-law confirmation.
overview: Council held a brief special meeting and dealt mainly with two development charge complaints, one for 15 Dellroy Avenue and one for a Highland Road property. Council agreed to adjourn the hearing on both until no later than March 30, 2026 {{vote:m1}}. The adjournment was referred from the Finance and Corporate Services Committee, and the complaints will return at a later meeting.

Council also authorized a closed meeting right after the special meeting to consider a matter of potential litigation {{vote:m2}}. The minutes report no outcome from that session, so nothing further is known publicly.

The Mayor announced that the next regular Council meeting, on Monday, March 2, 2026, will start at 4:00 p.m. instead of 7:00 p.m. A special Council or caucus meeting will follow if needed. Residents planning to attend or watch should note the earlier start. Council then passed its routine by-law confirming the day's proceedings and adjourned.

decisions.detail: Council granted the request in report FIN-2026-071 to adjourn the hearing on the development charge complaints for 15 Dellroy Avenue and a Highland Road property until no later than March 30, 2026.

debate: The transcript records no debate on the adjournment. It was moved and seconded as a referral from the Finance and Corporate Services Committee and carried.
The Mayor briefly asked the Clerk whether a specific adjournment date was needed. The Clerk apparently said no, and the matter went to a vote.
